subject: NeedleScope Hosted API: volume bounds & peak concurrency qualification
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Alex Patel <alex@needlescope.ai>, Priya Kapoor <priya@needlescope.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: NeedleScope Hosted API: volume bounds & peak concurrency qualification

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick post-call recap and explicit ask so we can size pricing bands and the pilot: 

Summary of what I captured from today:
- Primary workload: conversational assistant + short-form summarization for product support tickets.
- Current production target: ramp to steady-state in Q1 2027.

Can you confirm these three items so we can lock pricing ranges?
1) Expected monthly token volume (range if uncertain). e.g., pilot month 1, then months 2–6 and steady state.
2) Peak concurrency requirement (99th percentile TPS during business hours and peak spikes).
3) Target $/1M tokens you’re aiming for so we can map to our hosted bands.

We attached a quick pricing workbook and a SOC2 snapshot for procurement (pricing_workbook.xlsx; soc2-snapshot.pdf). Ben (cc) will run a quick cost simulation once we have your numbers.

Next steps: if you confirm the items above, we’ll return a 2-option pricing proposal (pilot band + commit band) and a draft SOW for signature.

Thanks — Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0193

---
Redwood Inference — Hosted API, Dedicated, Private deployments
From: Alex Patel <alex@needlescope.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Kapoor <priya@needlescope.ai>
Date: 2026-11-26T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: NeedleScope Hosted API: volume bounds & peak concurrency qualification

Sofia — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming numbers from our side (estimates, happy to firm up):

1) Monthly token volume (estimate ranges):
- Pilot (month 1): ~500k tokens (limited user cohort)
- Ramp (months 2–6): 3.5M–6M tokens / month
- Steady-state (target after Q1): ~8M–12M tokens / month

2) Peak concurrency (99th pct):
- Typical steady peak: ~40–60 TPS sustained for short windows (5–10 minutes).
- Occasional spikes: up to ~75 TPS for very short bursts (<2 minutes) during product launches.
- Average request payload: ~350 tokens in / 420 tokens out (round-trip ~770 tokens).

3) Budget target: we’re aiming at roughly $40 / 1M tokens for steady-state; pilot pricing can be higher. Procurement will want a clear run-rate example.

We can share a short sample of anonymized traffic if that helps for the cost sim. Also attaching a short draft SOW (pilot_sow.docx) — internal only until pricing is discussed.

— Alex
Alex Patel
Head of Integrations | NeedleScope Labs
alex@needlescope.ai

On Wed, Nov 25, 2026 at 3:02 PM Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick post-call recap...
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alex Patel <alex@needlescope.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-26T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: NeedleScope Hosted API: volume bounds & peak concurrency qualification

Alex / Sofia — looping in some quick pricing guidance based on Alex’s ranges. High-level options we can offer on Hosted API (ballpark, final numbers will depend on exact token composition and 99th-pt windows):

Option A (Commit band — recommended if you hit >=10M/mo): $35 / 1M tokens
- Includes reserved capacity, predictable latency, burst buffer for short spikes up to +25% of commit
- Intended for steady-state workloads; can add Dedicated if you need stronger isolation

Option B (Pilot / On-demand band): $45–55 / 1M tokens depending on peak TPS and request size
- Flexible, no minimum; best for month 1 and early ramp

Notes on peak TPS: from engineering — sustained 60 TPS with 770 token round-trip maps to different GPU footprints vs short 75 TPS bursts. If NeedleScope expects repeated 75+ TPS bursts, we’ll recommend a short burst add-on SKU to avoid throttling.

Ben will run a sample cost sim against your traffic profile (Alex’s provided averages) and put a sample invoice for the pilot + 3-month ramp. Sofia — I’ll attach the sim output to the proposal.

— Ben Carter
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

From: Alex Patel <alex@needlescope.ai>

Subject: Re: NeedleScope Hosted API: volume bounds & peak concurrency qualification

Thanks — Option A looks in-line with what procurement expects if we can hit the 10M threshold. Two quick asks before we proceed: 
1) Can you share a 6-month cost projection (pilot + ramp) that shows $/1M and monthly bill for the ranges I listed?
2) For the pilot, what SLA and rollback options exist if latency during spikes exceeds our internal thresholds?

We’ll move forward with a 1-month pilot (500k tokens) if the numbers align; procurement wants to see a sample invoice and the SOW with trial terms. Attaching pilot_sow.docx here (internal).

— Alex

Great — thanks for the clarity, Alex. Action items and next steps: 

1) Ben to deliver a 6-month cost projection + sample invoice by EOD tomorrow (includes pilot 500k, ramp months, and both Option A/B pricing bands).
2) I’ll share the pricing simulator link so you can tweak average tokens/request and see run-rate impact: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1a2B3cPricingSim

4) I’ll upload a draft SOW to DocuSign for review (https://app.docusign.com/samples/NDL-SOW-2026).

Proposed calendar: let’s reconvene on Tue, Dec 1 at 10:00 AM PT to review the projection and sign the pilot SOW if everything looks good. I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward to getting NeedleScope on a pilot.

— Sofia
